title: Kakutani from Brouwer via Approximate Selections

problemStatement.formal: \text{Prove kakutani\_finite\_dim from brouwer\_fpt via approximate selections}
problemStatement.plain: Prove Kakutani's fixed point theorem from Brouwer's FPT by constructing approximate continuous selections, applying Brouwer, and taking limits.
whyMatters: Key tool for Nash equilibrium existence
Fundamental result in topological fixed point theory

knowledge.progressSummary: SURVEYED: Built proof framework for Kakutani from Brouwer. Identified three independent axioms (Brouwer, approximate selections, sequential compactness). Framework has 2 sorries for the combination arguments. Main Mathlib gap: partition of unity for approximate selections.
builtItems: Defined IsApproxSelection for ε-approximate continuous selections
Axiomatized three key lemmas: Brouwer, approx selections, seq compactness
Created gallery entry with meta.json, index.ts
insights: Approximate selections (Cellina 1969) avoid triangulation machinery — cleaner than simplicial approximation
The proof factors into 3 independent axioms that can be proved separately
Main Mathlib gap: partition of unity for finite open covers of compact subsets of ℝⁿ
The combination argument (applying Brouwer + compactness + UHC) is the straightforward part
Brouwer's FPT in Mathlib is for closed balls; needs extension to general compact convex sets
mathlibGaps: Brouwer FPT for general compact convex sets (only closed balls in Mathlib)
Partition of unity construction for finite open covers in Euclidean space
Sequential compactness equivalence for compact metric spaces
